title: Projection coherence for every normalized strict-system presentation
statement: Let k be an algebraic closure of a finite field of characteristic p and let l be a prime distinct from p [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let f:X→Y be a separated finite-type morphism of finite-type k-schemes, and fix a compactification c [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Let t:Theory c l be any presentation of the actual ordinary and unbounded derived strict-system operations, with section-normalized ordinary restriction squares, their prescribed geometric adjunction mates, exact evaluation, and normalized scalar adjunctions [def-pur-etale-system-projection-data]. The coefficient sequences are inverse sequences of finite commutative rings, each level killed by a power of l, with arbitrary transitions. Then the scalar-adjunction mate q of the inverse proper/open restriction comparison evaluates, under t.supportEvaluation and t.scalarEvaluation, to compactScalarMap. For composable coefficient maps a and b, q(a≫b) equals t.path a b, the pasted projection word transported by the canonical balanced tensor associators. For the identity coefficient map, q followed by the support image of the scalar unit equals the scalar unit on the support functor. These are the three displayed formulas in the Lean attachment, as equalities of transformations on entire ordinary unbounded derived categories. No exceptional right adjoint or its evaluation comparison occurs.

source.place: Constructions 2.26 and 5.15, Lemma 5.16; presentation-independent normalization implicit in the coefficient projection construction.

proof.text: Choose the normalized reference presentation and its laws from [lem-pur-etale-system-coefficient-projection]. Compare its proper and open operations with those of the given t. Ordinary direct images have identical underlying section maps and structural coefficient maps: their structural maps agree on constant generators and hence by sheafification. Left-adjoint uniqueness therefore gives unit/counit-compatible comparisons of the inverse images and open extensions. The ordinary restriction and evaluation squares commute with these comparisons, since their prescribed section maps are identities. Their inverse-image mates, localized exact comparisons, and derived geometric mates consequently commute as well, by [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. Scalar left-adjoint uniqueness compares the normalized scalar models. Pasting these commuting squares transports the reference evaluated projection identity to t, and gives precisely the first displayed equation. No equality is inferred merely from equality after derived evaluation.

Use the comparisons with the reference presentation from step 1. Successive exact restriction has its canonical identity-on-sections compositor. Scalar adjoint uniqueness identifies the comparison for the composite extension with the balanced associators defined in t. Apply mate pasting to the ordinary proper and open restriction squares, then their prescribed localization and derived-mate equations: the two projection words are conjugate to the corresponding reference projection words. Transport the reference composition identity from [lem-pur-etale-system-coefficient-projection] through these isomorphisms. Naturality and cancellation of consecutive inverse comparisons give exactly q(a≫b)=t.path a b on entire derived categories.

For identity coefficients, the restriction unit has identity section maps. The scalar adjoint-uniqueness tensor unit is compatible with the comparisons of step 1. Transport the reference projection unit identity from [lem-pur-etale-system-coefficient-projection] and cancel the inverse comparisons. Equivalently transpose through the scalar adjunction and use its triangle identities. The result is the third displayed equation. The zero ring and empty schemes are included, because no cancellation by a nonzero scalar or positive rank is used.

lean.statement:
theorem etaleSystemProjectionPresentationCoherence
    (k : WeilConjectures.FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (l : ℕ) (hl : l.Prime) (hlp : l ≠ k.p)
    (X Y : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k.k)))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom] [QuasiCompact X.hom]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType Y.hom] [QuasiCompact Y.hom]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsSeparated f.left] [LocallyOfFiniteType f.left] [QuasiCompact f.left]
    (c : Compactification f.left) (t : Theory c l) :
      (∀ (B C : Coefficients.{u} l) (a : B.rings ⟶ C.rings) (n : ℕ)
        (M : Derived X.left B.rings),
        (scalarExtension (a.app (op n)).hom Y.left).map
            ((t.supportEvaluation B n).iso.inv.app M) ≫
          (t.scalarEvaluationY a n).iso.inv.app ((t.support B).F.obj M) ≫
          (t.evaluationY C n).E.map ((t.q a).app M) ≫
          (t.supportEvaluation C n).iso.hom.app ((t.scalarX a).model.T.obj M) ≫
          (rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactification
            (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (C.rings.obj (op n))) c).map
              ((t.scalarEvaluationX a n).iso.hom.app M) =
          (compactScalarMap (a.app (op n)).hom c).app ((t.evaluationX B n).E.obj M)) ∧
      (∀ (B C D : Coefficients.{u} l) (a : B.rings ⟶ C.rings) (b : C.rings ⟶ D.rings),
        t.q (a ≫ b) = t.path a b) ∧
      (∀ (B : Coefficients.{u} l) (M : Derived X.left B.rings),
        (t.q (𝟙 B.rings)).app M ≫
          (t.support B).F.map ((unit X.left B.rings (t.scalarX (𝟙 B.rings))).hom.app M) =
        (unit Y.left B.rings (t.scalarY (𝟙 B.rings))).hom.app ((t.support B).F.obj M))
